original_value: Breast tumor segmentation in medical images is a decisive step for diagnosis and treatment follow-up. Automating this challenging task helps radiologists to reduce the high manual workload of breast cancer analysis. In this paper, we propose two deep learning approaches to automate the breast tumor segmentation in dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) by building two fully convolutional neural networks (CNN) based on SegNet and U-Net. The obtained models can handle both detection and segmentation on each single DCE-MRI slice. In this study, we used a dataset of 86 DCE-MRIs, acquired before and after two cycles of chemotherapy, of 43 patients with local advanced breast cancer, a total of 5452 slices were used to train and validate the proposed models. The data were annotated manually by an experienced radiologist. To reduce the training time, a high-performance architecture composed of graphic processing units was used. The model was trained and validated, respectively, on 85% and 15% of the data. A mean intersection over union (IoU) of 68.88 was achieved using SegNet and 76.14% using U-Net architecture.

result.paraphrase: Breast tumor segmentation in medical images is a key step for diagnosis and treatment follow-up. Automating this demanding task can help radiologists reduce the heavy manual workload involved in breast cancer analysis. In this paper, we present two deep learning methods for automating breast tumor segmentation in dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) by constructing two fully convolutional neural networks (CNNs) based on SegNet and U-Net. The resulting models can perform both detection and segmentation on each individual DCE-MRI slice. For this study, we used 86 DCE-MRIs acquired before and after two chemotherapy cycles from 43 patients with locally advanced breast cancer; a total of 5452 slices were used to train and validate the proposed models. The data were manually annotated by an experienced radiologist. To shorten training time, a high-performance architecture made up of graphics processing units was employed. The model was trained and validated on 85% and 15% of the data, respectively. A mean intersection over union (IoU) of 68.88 was obtained with SegNet and 76.14% with the U-Net architecture.
